problem: The sentence 'Python's built-in error names end in Error' is stated as a rule, but several built-in exceptions do not end in Error (StopIteration, KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit). A student may conclude those are not exceptions at all.
fix: Say: 'Most of the built-in exceptions you will meet first end in Error: ZeroDivisionError, NameError, TypeError, ValueError. A few, such as KeyboardInterrupt and StopIteration, do not.'

problem: The answer fixes the reported line at 7 with certainty. On several Python 3 versions a missing colon is reported on the line after the faulty one, so the student's screen may say line 8. The teaching point (nothing runs, so only the syntax error is seen) is right, but the line number is stronger than the facts.
fix: Answer: 'Only a SyntaxError near line 7 is shown (some versions point at the following line). The file never runs, so the TypeError on line 4 is never reached. Fix the colon first, then the runtime error appears.'

problem: The answer tells the student to read the bottom line and the line above it, and stops there. In the stated situation the bottom frames are inside the library; the student can only edit the line at the top, so the answer is incomplete and may send them to fix code they do not own.
fix: Answer: 'Start at the bottom for the error name and message, then walk upward frame by frame. Keep going until you reach your own line at the top; the frames in between only show which library calls your line went through. The bug to fix is in your line, not in the library.'
